question: Should OpenClaw accept node-advertised, model-visible tools as a core Gateway/node protocol surface, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90431 be the implementation path after its blockers are resolved?
rationale: The feature crosses a node-to-model execution boundary, so source inspection cannot choose the permanent trust, policy, and plugin/core ownership model for maintainers.

options.title: Proceed Through Guarded Protocol
options.body: Use the open candidate PR or an equivalent narrow PR, but require provenance, allow/deny policy, reconnect cleanup, compatibility, docs, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Keep Wrapper Plugins For Now
options.body: Leave node tools behind plugin-owned wrappers until maintainers are ready to define and ship the node-to-model trust contract.

options.title: Reject Node-Declared Tools
options.body: Close this direction and ask integrations to remain plugins or ClawHub packages, accepting the current loopback complexity.

recommendation.title: Proceed Through Guarded Protocol
recommendation.body: Use the open candidate PR or an equivalent narrow PR, but require provenance, allow/deny policy, reconnect cleanup, compatibility, docs, and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the open implementation candidate and has the most direct recent history on the affected Gateway/node/tool protocol path.
